contentBlocks.body: A bare type parameter T could be anything, so inside the function you cannot read any property from it. A constraint, written T extends { id: string }, says T can be any type that has at least an id string. You gain access to item.id, and callers still get their full, specific type back instead of a trimmed-down one.

Compare with the non-generic version function byId(items: { id: string }[]). It accepts the same inputs, but the result only knows about id, so lookup.t1.done would be a compile error. The generic keeps the caller's type flowing through.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Inside function f<T>(item: T), why is item.id a compile error?

choices: T is unconstrained, so TypeScript cannot assume it has an id
item must be annotated as any first
payload.answer: T is unconstrained, so TypeScript cannot assume it has an id
payload.explanation: Add a constraint such as T extends { id: string } to allow reading id.

payload.text: function latest<T ____ { updatedAt: string }>(items: T[]): T

knowledgeItems.prompt: Given latest<T extends { updatedAt: string }>(items: T[]): T, what does latest(todos) return when todos is Todo[]?

payload.explanation: T is inferred as Todo from the argument; the constraint only limits which types are allowed.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Deduplicate synced records: for each id keep the version with the latest updatedAt (first wins on ties), in first-seen order, returning the caller's full objects.
